open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 address-space limit scope
open_points.text: address space by the parent, from outside the environment
open_points.question: To which process is the address-space limit applied, and is it installed before bubblewrap and Python start-up or only on the in-sandbox runner before loading the implementation?
options: Apply it to the bubblewrap child and everything it starts, including sandbox and interpreter start-up
Apply it to the in-sandbox runner after sandbox construction but before code loads
Apply it only while the implementation's run function executes
open_points.default_guess: Apply it to the in-sandbox runner after sandbox construction and before the implementation loads.

open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 failure to install limits and start probe
open_points.text: A runner that cannot set its limit exits before loading the code and the execution is crashed; the start probe (rule 8) runs the same runner, so a host where the limit cannot be set does not start the kernel.
open_points.question: What happens when the parent cannot install the address-space limit, and which memory and process-count values must the start probe attempt so that a successful probe establishes that every accepted contract bound can be installed?
options: Treat any address-limit installation failure as crashed, and probe at the release ceilings
Treat such a failure as resource_exhausted, and probe at the execution's requested bounds only when it runs
Refuse kernel start for any installation failure, without recording an execution
open_points.default_guess: Have the start probe install both limits at their release ceilings; classify a later unexpected installation failure as crashed before code loads.

open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 resource-limit outcome
open_points.text: a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, output_bytes) — resource_exhausted
open_points.question: Does an allocation or process-creation refusal count as a limit hit even when user code catches the resulting exception and returns conforming outputs, and if so, how must the runner communicate that hit so the parent can enforce the stated outcome precedence?
options: Every denied allocation or process creation counts and must be reported out of band, like a rule 4 trap
Only termination or another externally observable limit event counts; a caught denial does not
A caught denial counts only when the runner can distinguish it reliably, otherwise the returned result is evaluated normally
open_points.default_guess: Count every denied allocation or process creation and require the runner to report it through a channel user code cannot undo.
